entries.good_example: start_ns=$(date +%s%N); ./cmd; end_ns=$(date +%s%N); elapsed_ms=$(( (end_ns - start_ns) / 1000000 )); echo "Done in ${elapsed_ms}ms"
entries.rationale: Standard Unix timestamps (%s) are too coarse for script optimization. SS QLM requires nanosecond precision (%N) to accurately measure logic bottlenecks.

entries.good_example: benchmark_cmd() { local total=0; for i in {1..5}; do local t_start=$(date +%s%N); "$@"; local t_end=$(date +%s%N); total=$((total + (t_end - t_start))); done; echo "Average: $((total / 5 / 1000000))ms"; }
entries.rationale: Single runs are subject to OS noise and caching. SS QLM standardizes the 'Multi-Run Average' pattern to filter out anomalies and provide realistic performance data.
